text:
alex_k: Heads up — after the driver/CUDA patch rolled to 535.* on cluster-east we started seeing MIG profiles vanish on ~8 nodes. scheduler shows GPUs as unavailable (UUID mismatch).

mira_p: which nodes? 8 is a lot. region?

alex_k: east1-gpu-12, east1-gpu-15, east1-gpu-21, east1-gpu-22, east1-gpu-30, east1-gpu-31, east1-gpu-44, east1-gpu-45

chris_r: can you paste output of `nvidia-smi -L` and `nvidia-smi mig -lg` from one of the failing hosts? also `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`

alex_k: `nvidia-smi -L` shows physical devices but the MIG UUIDs don't match what the cluster has recorded (old UUIDs returned 0 results). `nvidia-smi mig -lg` returns "No MIG devices found" on those hosts. driver version shows: "NVIDIA-SMI 535.86  Driver Version: 535.86  CUDA Version: 12.2"

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-17T09:34:12 started: rolling-driver/535.86 -> cluster-east (8 nodes)

mira_p: did the nodes reboot as part of the deploy? MIG reconfig often needs a cold reset / firmware sync.

alex_k: yes, nodes rebooted. dmesg has repeated lines: "nvidia: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: MIG reconfigured, new UUID aa:bb:cc..." then later "MIG instance removed".

chris_r: sounds like the driver upgrade triggered a MIG firmware migration/reset and assigned new MIG instance UUIDs. scheduler's persistent annotations still point at old UUIDs -> mismatch. two short fixes: 1) recreate MIG profiles to match desired shapes and let scheduler pick new UUIDs, 2) map the new UUIDs back into our node labels (if possible) so pod requests match.

tara_ops: what's the customer impact? are jobs failing or just pending? cost hit if we lose density.

alex_k: a bunch of batch jobs pending; autoscaler is spinning up extra nodes in other regions to compensate, already +3 extra GPUs (cost delta ~+$2.1k/day projected if not fixed).

mira_p: can we run `nvidia-smi mig -cgi` to recreate profiles non-destructively? IIRC you must `-C` to create, but it's destructive to existing MIG instances. we should drain the nodes first.

chris_r: plan: 1) drain affected nodes (no new pods), 2) snapshot current scheduler annotations, 3) on a single node run `nvidia-smi mig -lgdev` to inspect dev ids, then run `nvidia-smi mig -C -i 0 -g 1g.10gb` (example) to recreate required profiles, 4) update k8s node labels to point to new UUIDs, 5) uncordon. I'll prepare a small mapping script to extract new UUIDs and patch node objects.

alex_k: trying a dry-run on east1-gpu-12 now, will post logs.

alex_k: [paste] `# nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-1111-2222-3333)
# nvidia-smi mig -lg
No MIG devices found
# dmesg | tail
[  12.345678] nvidia: MIG instance 0000:3b:00.0:0 removed (old UUID GPU-aaaa-bbbb)
`

mira_p: if `nvidia-smi -L` shows the physical GPU but mig list empty, MIG got reset. recreation required. Good you're draining. remember to restart `nvidia-persistenced` after reconfig.

chris_r: I'm pushing a small patch to the rollout script to abort and flag nodes if `nvidia-smi mig -lg` suddenly goes from >0 -> 0 during deploy. also adding a post-driver-check that verifies node label UUIDs vs `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=gpu_uuid --format=csv,noheader`. helps prevent silent UUID drift.

tara_ops: approve that patch. also open a billing alert so finance sees the temporary autoscaler spend.

alex_k: update: recreated MIG profiles on 3 nodes, mapping script found new UUIDs and patched k8s nodes, two pods resumed. continuing for rest. will follow up with a postmortem and rollback option if more nodes break. :thumbsup:

mira_p: long-term: vendor ticket? we should add a canary gate: perform driver upgrade on 1 rack, validate MIG persistence across reboot before rolling the rest.

chris_r: noted. filing a bug in infra repo and I'll add an e2e check. thanks all.
